why_a_get_pays: The body scan is method-gated to POST/PUT/PATCH (nrgi.3), so a GET has no body to scan. The QUERY STRING is scanned for every method above that gate, because a GET carrying SQLi in its query must still be detected. This is the read-path instance of the EM-9/EM-10 regime finding.

prefilter_property.statement: Asserted against the EXACT byte string sent, not assumed from the choice of words. The literal set's shortest entry is b"or" - TWO bytes - so an entirely benign search term containing "reports" is admitted and the full regex runs.

scan_cost.ceiling_basis: absolute, chosen BEFORE measurement, never relaxed
scan_cost.protocol: best-of-N with gc.collect(), per 4.4's microbenchmark protocol

transfer_from_body_scan.note: Carrying EM-10's per-KB rate across to a GET would OVER-PREDICT by a wide margin, because a 4 KB query string is small in absolute terms. The two regimes are the same code but different magnitudes, so a rate does not transfer and this measures it.

excluded: No 6.7 us figure appears anywhere in this artefact. That number came from a stale audit and S-7 (m1gm) exists to correct it.
